quests.instruction: Apple slices turn brown when they sit out for a while. Which liquid, brushed on top, helps keep them looking fresh?
quests.hint: It has a sharp, sour taste.
quests.explanation: The acid in lemon juice slows down the browning. Milk and oil do not protect apple slices in the same way.
quests.funFact: Apples, bananas and pears turn brown because a substance inside them reacts with oxygen in the air.

quests.instruction: Cheese is rubbed against a tool with lots of small sharp holes and falls off in thin strips. What is this job called?
quests.hint: It is how pasta gets its cheesy topping.
quests.explanation: Grating shreds food into small pieces. Graters are sharp, so a grown-up should help.
quests.funFact: Grated cheese melts faster than a whole block because the pieces are thin.

quests.instruction: Two eggs are boiled, one for a few minutes and one for much longer. What is different about the egg that boiled longer?
quests.hint: Heat keeps changing the egg as time passes.
quests.explanation: The longer an egg cooks, the more its yolk sets, so it ends up firm.
quests.funFact: Cooks use timers because even one extra minute changes how firm an egg turns out.

quests.instruction: Which tiny, friendly living things turn milk into yogurt?
quests.hint: They work while the milk is kept warm.
quests.explanation: Friendly bacteria feed on the sugar in milk and make it thick and tangy. Yeast is used for bread and seeds grow into plants.
quests.funFact: Yogurt is a fermented food, like cheese, sauerkraut and sourdough bread.

quests.instruction: When cheesemakers thicken milk, it separates into solid lumps and a watery liquid. What are the solid lumps called?
quests.hint: Cheese is made from them.
quests.explanation: The lumps are called curds, and the liquid is called whey. The curds are pressed and shaped into cheese.
quests.funFact: The leftover whey is also used in some foods and drinks.

quests.instruction: Cucumbers are soaked in vinegar or salty water to make pickles. What does this help them do?
quests.hint: Ask yourself how long a jar of pickles lasts in the fridge.
quests.explanation: Salt and vinegar make it hard for spoilage germs to grow, so pickles last longer.
quests.funFact: Many cultures pickle foods, from Indian mango pickle to Japanese tsukemono.

quests.instruction: Which part of a recipe tells you everything you need to gather before you start?
quests.hint: It is usually near the top of the page.
quests.explanation: The ingredients list names what you need and how much. The steps tell you what to do, and the title names the dish.
quests.funFact: Many recipes list the ingredients in the order you will use them.

quests.instruction: A recipe says to heat the oven before mixing the batter. Why?
quests.correctAnswer: So it is hot when the batter is ready 🔥
options: So it is hot when the batter is ready 🔥
So the oven can be washed out first 🧽
So the batter stays very cold and thick 🧊
quests.hint: Think about how long a cold oven takes to warm up.
quests.explanation: Ovens take time to heat up, so starting early means the batter can bake right away. A grown-up should always handle the oven.
quests.funFact: Most ovens take around ten to fifteen minutes to heat up.

quests.instruction: Which kitchen tool counts the minutes so you know when baking time is up?
quests.hint: It rings when the time is finished.
quests.explanation: A timer reminds cooks when time is up, so food is not undercooked or burnt.
quests.funFact: Cooks often set a timer for each step so nothing gets overcooked.

quests.instruction: Cookie dough needs something that works like glue to hold everything together. Which ingredient does that job?
quests.hint: It is sticky when it is raw.
quests.explanation: Eggs bind the other ingredients so the cookie keeps its shape. Salt adds flavor and chocolate chips are an extra.
quests.funFact: Eggs also help cakes rise and stay moist.

quests.instruction: A pancake recipe needs milk, but a family does not drink cow's milk. Which could they use instead?
quests.hint: Many plant drinks look and pour like milk.
quests.explanation: Plant milks made from oats, soy or almonds can replace cow's milk in many recipes. Honey and cheese would change the recipe a lot.
quests.funFact: People choose plant milks for many reasons, including allergies, beliefs and taste.

quests.instruction: A soup tastes flat and bland. Which small addition would make its flavor stand out?
quests.hint: Cooks add it a little at a time.
quests.explanation: A small amount of salt brings out the flavors in food. Ice would water the soup down and flour would thicken it.
quests.funFact: Too much salt hides other tastes, so cooks add it slowly and taste as they go.

quests.instruction: Carrots are cooked in a hot oven until their edges turn brown. How does their taste change?
quests.hint: Look at the browned edges.
quests.explanation: Roasting browns a vegetable's natural sugars and makes it taste sweeter.
quests.funFact: Roasting also dries the surface, which gives vegetables slightly crisp edges.

quests.instruction: Crunchy cereal flakes sit in a bowl of milk for ten minutes. What happens to them?
options: They turn into tiny blocks of ice 🧊
quests.hint: Dry things soak up liquid.
quests.explanation: Dry flakes soak up the milk, so they lose their crunch and get soft.
quests.funFact: That is why many people eat cereal quickly, while it is still crunchy.

quests.instruction: What cooking method keeps a liquid just below a full boil, with small gentle bubbles?
quests.hint: Soups and stews often cook this way for a long time.
quests.explanation: Simmering is a gentle heat that cooks food slowly. Frying uses hot oil and freezing makes food cold.
quests.funFact: Gentle simmering helps tough foods like beans turn tender without breaking apart.

quests.instruction: Which kitchen job removes the skin from a potato or an apple?
quests.hint: It takes off the outside layer.
quests.explanation: Peeling removes the skin, usually with a peeler. Ask a grown-up to help with sharp tools.
quests.funFact: The skins of many fruits and vegetables are safe to eat, and some people leave them on.

quests.instruction: Lemonade starts by squeezing lemons. What do we collect from them?
quests.hint: It is the liquid inside.
quests.explanation: Squeezing presses out the juice that is inside the fruit. Seeds and leaves are not what we want.
quests.funFact: A lemon gives more juice if you roll it on the counter before you squeeze it.

quests.instruction: Boiled potatoes are pressed until they are soft and lumpy. What is this job called?
quests.hint: Ask yourself what you do to a banana with a fork.
quests.explanation: Mashing squashes soft food into a thick mixture. Grating makes thin strips and squeezing presses out juice.
quests.funFact: Different countries add their own touches to mashed potatoes, such as the cabbage in Irish colcannon.

quests.instruction: A bowl of soup is steaming hot. What should you do before eating it?
quests.hint: Hot food can burn your mouth.
quests.explanation: Waiting lets the soup cool to a safe temperature. Hot food can burn your tongue.
quests.funFact: Some soups, like Spanish gazpacho, are meant to be served cold.

quests.instruction: Dough is pressed, folded and turned again and again by hand. What is this job called?
quests.hint: It makes the dough stretchy.
quests.explanation: Kneading stretches the dough so it can trap gas bubbles and become chewy.
quests.funFact: Well-kneaded dough springs back when you poke it.

quests.instruction: Cooked pasta is poured into a colander, a bowl full of holes. What drains away?
quests.hint: The holes let liquid pass through.
quests.explanation: The cooking water runs out through the holes and the pasta stays behind. Oil and sauce are added later, not drained. A grown-up should pour hot water.
quests.funFact: The starchy cooking water from pasta is sometimes kept to make sauces smoother.

quests.instruction: Which food is made by cooking chopped apples until they are soft and mashing them smooth?
quests.hint: It is soft enough to eat with a spoon.
quests.explanation: Cooking breaks apples down into applesauce. Juice is squeezed out and pie has a crust.
quests.funFact: Applesauce is often used in baking to replace some of the butter or oil.

quests.instruction: Which two simple ingredients form the base of most dried pasta dough?
quests.hint: They are also the start of bread dough.
quests.explanation: Pasta dough is mostly flour and water. Honey, oil, rice and milk are not its base.
quests.funFact: Dry pasta is usually made from durum wheat, a very hard type of wheat.

quests.instruction: Fresh tomatoes are cooked and crushed until they become a thick red mixture. What have they become?
quests.hint: Ask yourself what goes on pasta.
quests.explanation: Cooking breaks tomatoes down and lets extra water escape, which leaves a thick sauce.
quests.funFact: Cooking down a sauce makes the tomato flavor stronger because the water evaporates.

quests.instruction: Which list shows how to make lemonade, in the right order?
quests.correctAnswer: Squeeze the lemons, add water and sugar, stir and chill 🍋
options: Squeeze the lemons, add water and sugar, stir and chill 🍋
Add water and sugar, stir and chill, squeeze the lemons 🍋
Stir and chill, squeeze the lemons, add water and sugar 🍋
quests.hint: You need juice before you can mix it.
quests.explanation: The lemons are squeezed first, then water and sugar are added, and last the lemonade is stirred and chilled.
quests.funFact: Lemonade tastes best when the sugar is fully dissolved, so stir until you cannot see it.

quests.instruction: Put these pasta steps in the right order. Which list is correct?
quests.correctAnswer: Heat the water until it bubbles, add the pasta, drain it in a colander 🍝
options: Add the pasta, drain it in a colander, heat the water until it bubbles 🍝
Heat the water until it bubbles, add the pasta, drain it in a colander 🍝
Drain it in a colander, add the pasta, heat the water until it bubbles 🍝
quests.hint: The water must be hot before the pasta goes in.
quests.explanation: The water is heated first, then the pasta cooks in it, and last the water is drained away. A grown-up should handle boiling water.
quests.funFact: The cooking time is printed on the pasta package.

quests.instruction: What is the correct order for making scrambled eggs?
quests.correctAnswer: Crack the eggs, whisk them, cook them in a pan 🍳
options: Cook them in a pan, crack the eggs, whisk them 🍳
Whisk them, cook them in a pan, crack the eggs 🍳
Crack the eggs, whisk them, cook them in a pan 🍳
quests.hint: You cannot whisk eggs that are still in their shells.
quests.explanation: The eggs are cracked into a bowl, whisked and then cooked. A grown-up should handle the hot pan.
quests.funFact: Eggs keep cooking from the pan's heat even after they come off the stove.

quests.instruction: Which of these changes is caused by cooling, not by heating?
quests.hint: Think about the freezer.
quests.explanation: Water freezes when it gets cold. Butter melts and eggs set when they get hot.
quests.funFact: Freezing is a way to keep food fresh for longer.

quests.instruction: A cook wants potatoes with golden, crisp edges. Which method works best?
quests.hint: Dry heat browns the outside.
quests.explanation: Dry oven heat browns and crisps potatoes. Soaking and mashing make them wet or soft.
quests.funFact: Potatoes brown in the oven because their natural sugars change color in the heat.

quests.instruction: A baker forgot one ingredient and the dough stayed flat and heavy. Which ingredient was probably missing?
quests.hint: It makes tiny bubbles of gas.
quests.explanation: Without yeast no gas bubbles form, so the dough cannot puff up.
quests.funFact: Some flatbreads are made without yeast on purpose, so they stay thin.
